# Recipe — add an event

## 0. First, prove you want an event at all

| You want… | Use | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Something **done** | **Call the service.** | You get a return value, an error path, and compile-time checking. |
| To announce something that **already happened**, and you neither know nor care who reacts | **Publish a fact.** | Decoupling is the point. |

**An event is a past-tense fact, never a command** (rule #1). `ShowDialogEvent` and `PlaySfxEvent`
are banned: they are service calls that have thrown away every guarantee. Want a dialog shown? Call
`IDialogService`. Want a sound? Call `IAudioService`.

Name the type as a completed fact: `MatchEnded`, `CurrencyGranted`, `SceneChanged` — never
`ShowX`, `PlayX`, `DoX`.

**A new event type is a spine change** (`AGENTS.framework.md` §6) — route it.

## 1. Edit the manifest

`Tools/Codegen/Manifests/Events/game.events.json` — append one entry:

```json
{
  "name": "ShopPurchased",
  "order": 3,
  "summary": "A shop item was bought and its grants were applied.",
  "params": [
    { "name": "ItemId", "type": "string" },
    { "name": "Price",  "type": "long" }
  ]
}
```

Params become named, typed constructor parameters on a generated record.

## 2. Generate

```
Framework/Codegen/Generate
```

`Assets/<Sku>/Gen/GameEvents.gen.cs` gains the record. **Never hand-edit a `.gen.cs` file.**

## 3. Register the broker — this step cannot be skipped

**MessagePipe has no source generator.** Every event type needs one explicit line, and that line
lives **only** in a file under `Installers/`:

```csharp
builder.RegisterMessageBroker<ShopPurchased>(new MessagePipeOptions());
```

A `RegisterMessageBroker<T>` anywhere outside `Installers/` **fails the CI grep by `file:line`**.
This is permanent boilerplate; no upstream relief is coming.

## 4. Publish and subscribe

Publish from the owner of the fact — the thing that made it true. Subscribe in whichever scope
cares; the subscription dies with that scope (`architecture-map.md` §2), so there is nothing to
unsubscribe manually.

**Gameplay never calls `IAnalytics` directly.** A forwarder maps the domain fact to a typed
analytics event. Keep that direction: fact in gameplay → forwarder → analytics.

## 5. Gate

```sh
Tools/Build/pf-build.sh codegen --check
sh Tools/CI/greps.sh source            # MessagePipe registration outside Installers/
```

## Framework facts already defined

`Runtime/Domain/Gen/GameEvents.gen.cs`: `CurrencyGranted` · `AdShown` · `AdRewarded` · `AdFailed` ·
`PurchaseSucceeded` · `PurchaseFailed` · `PurchaseRestored` · `SceneChanged` · `DialogOpened` ·
`DialogClosed`.

Domain facts published by framework services: `WalletChanged` · `ConsentChanged` · `SceneChange` ·
`DialogChange` · `AdVisibilityChanged` · `RemoteConfigFetched`. Subscribe to these rather than
inventing a parallel event.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| Nothing receives the publish | No `RegisterMessageBroker<T>` for that type. |
| CI names a `file:line` for MessagePipe | The registration is outside `Installers/`. Move it. |
| Review rejects the event | The name is imperative — it is a command, not a fact. |
| A subscription outlives its screen | It was taken in the wrong scope. Subscribe in the scope that should own it. |
